diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is a direct combination of \Cref{a18} and \Cref{a50}.

issues.failure_explanation:
Theorem 1.4 has several independent defects: (1) The measure $
u$ appearing in the Gram matrix $G$ and max norm $\gamma$ is never defined or quantified anywhere in the statement or preceding text. (2) The conclusion provides an asymptotic rate for the condition number $\kappa(V) = \|V\| \|V^{-1}\|$, but the proof (which simply cites Lemma 2.2 / \Cref{a18} and Lemma 5.2 / \Cref{a50}) only bounds $\|V^{-1}\|$; the paper establishes no upper or lower bounds on $\|V^{(p_0,\ldots,p_n)}\|$ for general polynomial bases. (3) Lemma 2.2 bounds $\|V^{-1}\|$ in terms of $\max_k \|L_k\|_{\supp(
u)}$, whereas Lemma 5.2 provides estimates for $\max_k \|L_k\|_{\supp(\mu)}$; since $\supp(
u)$ is not assumed or specified to equal $\supp(\mu)$, the two lemmas cannot be combined to deduce the theorem.

failure_location.quote: Let $p_0,\ldots,p_n$ form a basis of degree $\le n$ polynomials, with Gram matrix $G=\bmat{\inr{p_j}{p_k}_\nu}_{0\le j,k\le n}$ and max norm $\gamma=\max_{0\le j\le d}\magn{p_j(z)}_{\supp(\nu)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must define $\nu$, specify its relationship to $\mu$ (e.g., $\supp(\nu) = \supp(\mu)$), provide separate matching upper and lower bounds for the operator norm $\|V^{(p_0,\ldots,p_n)}\|$, and repair the proof of Lemma 5.2.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 1.4 is mathematically ill-defined and its stated bound on the condition number $\kappa(V^{(p_0,\dots,p_n)})$ is completely unsupported as written.
issues.title: Undefined measure, missing norm bounds, and support mismatch in Theorem 1.4
issues.why_classification: Theorem 1.4 is one of the main general theorems of the paper. Repairing it requires formulating missing definitions, proving bounds on the norm of general Vandermonde-like matrices, and establishing a valid connection between the measure $\nu$ and the potential-theoretic measure $\mu$.

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of the lower bound of Lemma 5.2, $z_-'$ (defined as $z_-^{(k)} = \argmin_{z\in\supp(\mu)} U^{\mu_k}(z)$) is the minimizer of $U^{\mu_k}$ over $\supp(\mu)$. The inequality $U^{\mu_k}(z_-^{(k)}) \le U^{\mu_k}(a)$ holds only if $a \in \supp(\mu)$. However, $a$ is chosen from $\ball(z_-, (n+1)^{1/2}r) \setminus \bigcup_{j=0}^n \ball(z_j, r) \subset \mathbb{C}$ via a 2D Lebesgue area argument. When $\supp(\mu)$ has empty 2D interior (for example, when $\mu$ is supported on an arc of the unit circle, the principal application highlighted in Remark 1.5), $\supp(\mu)$ has zero 2D Lebesgue measure, so the area argument does not ensure $a \in \supp(\mu)$. If $a \notin \supp(\mu)$, $U^{\mu_k}(z_-^{(k)}) \le U^{\mu_k}(a)$ fails because $U^{\mu_k}(z) \to -\infty$ as $|z| \to \infty$. In addition, in the proof of the upper bound, Lemma 5.1 is applied at $z = z_-^{(k)}$ with $\eps' = \min(\eps, (\beta\ks/2\rho_1)^{1/\beta})$ without establishing that $\dist(z_-^{(k)}, \supp(\mu_k)) \ge \eps'$, which is a required premise of Lemma 5.1.

failure_location.quote:
We pick $a$ to be any element of the set
\[\ball(z_-,(n+1)^{1/2}r)\backslash\bigcup_{j=0}^n\ball(z,r)\]
for $r=\frac1{2R}(\eps')^2$, which is nonempty by considering the areas of each ball.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict $\supp(\mu)$ to sets where relative neighborhood non-emptiness can be ensured, construct a point $a \in \supp(\mu)$ away from $S$, and establish an a priori lower bound on $\dist(z_-^{(k)}, \supp(\mu_k))$.
issues.overall_effect: Both the upper and lower bounds of Lemma 5.2 are mathematically unestablished, invalidating the general logarithmic potential rate estimates for Vandermonde-like matrices.
issues.title: Invalid test point selection and unverified distance hypothesis in Lemma 5.2
issues.why_classification: Lemma 5.2 is the core technical result of Section 5. The failures involve missing essential geometric hypotheses on the support of $\mu$ and unverified premises in potential-theoretic estimates that require substantially new arguments to resolve.
